name: The Rolling Stones
hook: Studied American blues records closely enough to become, for a while, the most dangerous-seeming band in Britain.
blurb: The Rolling Stones formed in London in 1962 around Brian Jones's classified ad for blues musicians. They built their early sound on close, deliberate study of Chess Records blues artists like Muddy Waters, who they were even named after, and of American blues and R&B records that were hard to find in Britain. They took it more seriously, as musicians, than the press's 'good-time' image of the scene suggested, which makes them a clear example of how the British R&B scene worked. They became Britain's other essential 1960s band, cast as the dangerous, rebellious counterpart to the more approachable Beatles. Brian Jones, the band's founder, was pushed out in 1969 amid drug and health problems and drowned weeks later.

signatureTracks.title: (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The fuzz-guitar riff that, alongside the Kinks' "You Really Got Me" the year before, helped establish distortion as a hit-single hook rather than a mistake.

signatureTracks.title: Come On
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Their debut single, a Chuck Berry cover, showing the direct blues-and-R&B-covers starting point before the band developed its own writing voice.
